Pakistan will use “whatever means are available” to defend Saudi Arabia against Iran-backed Houthi rebels, the country’s defense minister said Tuesday, offering one of Islamabad’s clearest indications yet that it could become directly involved in the widening regional conflict.

Defense Minister Khawaja Muhammad Asif declined to say whether Pakistani forces had already participated in airstrikes. He said, however, that Pakistan’s military capabilities would be available to Saudi Arabia under a new mutual defense pact with Saudi Arabia and Turkey.

“I’m not going into detail, but obviously when I say that we are bound by this arrangement to defend Saudi Arabia, that means whatever means are available at our disposal, they’ll be available to Saudi Arabia also. I think that’s a categoric statement,” Asif told reporters during a visit to Rome when asked whether Pakistan had been involved in airstrikes against Iranian operators in Yemen.

His response did not explicitly confirm Pakistani participation in any strikes. He also did not say whether Saudi Arabia, which has been repeatedly attacked by the Houthis in recent weeks, had asked for assistance.

Military commanders recently met

His comments came days after the army chiefs of Pakistan, Turkey and Saudi Arabia met in Riyadh to discuss responses to Houthi attacks.

Asif said the Houthis had intensified missile and drone attacks on Saudi Arabia and expanded their control along Yemen’s Red Sea coast.

The Houthis recently captured the strategic port city of Mokha and several Red Sea islands, extending their reach toward the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, a maritime route through which about 12% of global trade passes. They, along with allied militias in Iraq, also have attacked Saudi oil facilities and sought to prevent Saudi tankers from using the strait.

New alliance is still taking shape

Asif described the Houthis as aggressors and said Pakistan’s commitment to Saudi Arabia was unambiguous.

“Any enemy of Saudi Arabia is enemy of Pakistan. That should be very clear,” he said.

Saudi Arabia, Pakistan, and Turkey signed the Mecca Joint Defense Agreement on Aug. 7, declaring that an attack on one member would be treated as an attack on all three. The countries have described the pact as defensive and said it is not directed against any particular state.

The agreement brings together oil-rich Saudi Arabia, NATO member Turkey and nuclear-armed Pakistan. Asif did not mention nuclear weapons or suggest they were part of Pakistan’s commitment to Saudi Arabia.

The fighting between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis has created an early test for the alliance. The pact’s full text has not been released, and its command and operational structures are still being developed. Asif said the three countries were establishing a secretariat and putting the alliance’s framework in place.

Other countries have expressed interest in joining, he said, but there were no immediate plans to expand the alliance.

Asif said the alliance reflected a belief among its members that existing security arrangements had failed to protect Gulf countries as the conflict involving Iran spread across the region.

“Once you start a conflict, you cannot control the outcome of that conflict. You cannot control the trajectory of that conflict,” he said.

Pakistan retains ties with Iran

Iran has long supplied the Houthis with weapons and other assistance, though Tehran denies directing their military operations. Asif suggested the Houthis and some Iraqi militias might now act with substantial independence from Iran.

“Some of these proxies, they become rogue,” he said.

Despite Pakistan’s willingness to support Saudi Arabia militarily, Asif said Islamabad also was pressing for negotiations to end the broader conflict involving Iran and supported reviving a negotiated agreement over Tehran’s nuclear program.

Pakistan sought to establish itself as a mediator earlier this year, working with other countries in the region to end the conflict. While indirect talks between the U.S. and Iran have resumed through mediators, Asif provided no details on Pakistan's involvement in the latest efforts.

In April, Pakistan hosted rare direct talks between Iran and the United States in Islamabad. The two sides reached an interim agreement in June and committed to trying to reach a final deal within 60 days, but the deadline passed after hostilities resumed.

Top diplomats from Pakistan, Turkey and Saudi Arabia also met recently on the sidelines of the U.N. General Assembly to discuss implementing the new defense pact and coordinating a response to attacks targeting Mecca and other sites in Saudi Arabia.

While congressional Republicans block efforts to ban Donald Trump from demolishing the Kennedy Center, Department of Justice lawyers argue that the Trump-dominated institution is “already in a state of collapse both financially and physically” and nearly out of money to pay its bills.

On Monday night, Republican Sen. Mike Lee blocked bipartisan legislation to prevent the Trump administration from demolishing the venue after lawmakers drafted a bill in response to apparent threats that the building could be knocked down if the president isn’t allowed to add his name to it.

The Justice Department, meanwhile, told a federal appeals court that the beleaguered institution is “dangerously dilapidated, outdated and decrepit” while its finances are “equally in disrepair.”

On September 17, a federal judge ordered the Trump administration to provide at least 30 days’ notice before making any physical changes to the Kennedy Center — including demolishing it — after the Trump-controlled board voted to shutter the venue for repairs.

The vote followed a judge’s ruling that blocked the Kennedy Center from adding the president’s name to the building after he repeatedly tried to rename the memorial after himself.

open image in gallery The Trump administration says the Kennedy Center is ‘in a state of collapse’ as it fights to put the president’s name on the building — while his allies in Congress reject attempts to prevent him from demolishing it altogether ( Reuters )

Kennedy Center officials insist that the venue is only “temporarily” closing to assess the “advanced deterioration,” fueling speculation that the president could try to tear it down altogether.

“Like many arts and entertainment facilities, the Center has been losing tens of millions of dollars each and every year for decades, and it is projected to lose around $100 million per year long into the future,” government lawyers wrote Tuesday.

“In short, both physically and financially, the Kennedy Center is in critical condition,” they added. “To bring this sick and poorly run facility back to health will require time, energy, talent, and large amounts of money.”

Congress appropriated roughly $258 million for capital restoration projects and renovations at the Kennedy Center last year. The Trump administration’s takeover, meanwhile, put the venue on track to a projected $23 million deficit, as ticket sales plunged and subscriptions fell under the leadership change.

Without “appropriate recognition” — such as putting Trump’s name on the building — the Kennedy Center will be “a financially insolvent facility and a decrepit, dilapidated, crumbling building, that is bleeding hundreds of millions of dollars in losses and that continues to race toward physical and financial ruin,” according to the government.

open image in gallery Trump was seen on Air Force One reviewing images that appear to say ‘Kennedy Center Demolition’ after the venue’s board voted to close down following a judge’s order that blocks the president from renaming it after himself ( AFP/Getty )

“The stakes are existential,” lawyers added. “Just this month, the Kennedy Center was only able to pay its bills thanks to [$17 million] raised by President Trump that were infused into the Kennedy Center account to keep it afloat.”

Those funds are “fast being expended” and will “dry up” without the president' s support, according to the filing.

Without Trump, the Kennedy Center will “continue its deterioration into an unsafe structure that will eventually collapse, with a determination to follow on how to proceed, and what to do with the site.”

Last month, after filing several court documents using increasingly hyperbolic and ominous language to keep Trump’s name on the building, the Justice Department floated the possibility that the building could be demolished altogether.

Bipartisan legislation spearheaded by Democratic Sen. Jeff Merkley and Republican Sen. Lisa Murkowski sought to ban the demolition of presidential memorials. The senators lead the appropriations subcommittee that oversees funding for the center, the Interior Department and the National Park Service.

They sought to pass the bill by unanimous consent on Monday night, which would allow quick passage of a motion unless a single senator objects.

But Lee, a key Trump ally in the Senate, rejected the attempt.

“Trump’s threats to tear down the Kennedy Center — all because the law says he can’t put his name on the building — are straight out of the authoritarian playbook and should infuriate every American who values our history and the rule of law,” Merkley said in a statement.

Rep. Chellie Pingree, who is sponsoring a House version of the bill, said Trump’s threats are “beyond the pale.”

“This bill establishes a simple safeguard: if Congress created the designation, only an act of Congress can authorize its demolition,” she said.

News.title: How vaccines and antibiotics can beat some cancers
News.content:
At least one in eight cancers worldwide are caused by viruses and bacteria, according to a new study published in The Lancet.

An estimated 2.3 million new cancer cases in 2024 – out of a total of 20 million recorded worldwide – were caused by common infections, almost all of which could have been prevented with treatments such as antibiotics or vaccines.

Almost half of infection-linked cancers, around 760,000 cases, were caused by H. pylori, a bacterium that infects the stomach, researchers from the International Agency for Research on Cancer found.

The pathogen, which is typically ingested through contaminated food and water and is carried by around 60 per cent of the world’s population at any given time, can remain relatively undetected in the gut for between 20 and 40 years without causing any symptoms.

If left untreated, it can trigger chronic inflammation in the stomach and cellular mutations that, in some cases, lead to gastric cancer.

Cases of stomach cancer linked to H. pylori are particularly common in East Asia, where roughly 80 per cent of the population carries the bacterium. This is due in part to the prevalence of a more aggressive strain of the pathogen, known as CagA, which is endemic to the region.

East Asian diets – which typically include salty, pickled or smoked foods – can also damage the stomach’s protective lining and accelerate the inflammatory processes that can contribute to stomach cancer, researchers have found.

While H. pylori infection is treatable with a course of antibiotics, its symptoms often mimic those of other digestive problems and can be difficult to distinguish without testing.

This means the infection can remain undetected for years, allowing inflammation and damage to progress.

News.title: ‘Pooled’ TB testing could save money and improve diagnosis, study finds
News.content:
Mixing phlegm samples from multiple patients in “pooled tests” for tuberculosis could halve costs and help find millions of missing cases, according to a major new study.

While most advances in fighting TB come with a large price tag, the shift in strategy could dramatically boost access to diagnosis and save money, experts said.

TB is the deadliest single infection globally, killing around 1.3m people every year, despite being both preventable and curable.

The gold standard in diagnosis is rapid molecular testing, which detects genetic material from the bacteria causing TB in patient sputum samples within hours. But each sample needs a specialist diagnostic cartridge that costs around US$8, beyond the budget of many poorer countries even before recent aid cuts.

In a pooled test, samples from multiple individuals are tested in one cartridge. If the result is negative then all of them are reported to be negative, but if the result is positive each is re-tested individually.

Results published in The Lancet Global Health found the strategy, with up to four patients in each pool, used half as many cartridges as individual testing – 7,028 compared to 14,362. It detected 84.9 per cent of people with TB compared with 88 per cent for individual testing.

The study involved more than 14,000 people whose symptoms suggested TB in Bangladesh, Brazil, Cameroon, Kenya, Malawi, Nigeria and Vietnam.

News.title: UK borrowing costs hit highest level since 2007
News.content:
Britain’s borrowing costs hit their highest level since 2007 after Middle East tensions pushed oil prices above $108.

Yields on 10-year gilts, which determine the price the treasury pays to borrow money, rose above 5.43pc on Monday, before edging back to 5.42pc.

These are levels not seen in almost two decades, underlining the challenge facing John Healey as he prepares for next month’s Budget.

The Chancellor is coming under pressure to slash spending or raise taxes to bring Britain’s borrowing costs under control, against a backdrop of growing debt and rising inflation.

The surge in 10-year gilt yields pushes them above the 19-year high of 5.41pc recorded earlier this month, threatening to put a dent in Mr Healey’s fiscal headroom – a self-imposed guardrail to guide public spending.

Economists said high costs reflect the scale of Britain’s near-£3tn national debt and the rise in inflation facing the country.

“The uncomfortable truth for the PM and his Chancellor, John Healey ... is that the wide spread of gilt yields over peers is fair, in our view, given the UK’s dire fiscal position and the inflationary pressures stemming from high energy prices,” said Elliott Jordan-Doak, at Pantheon Macroeconomics.

“Gilt yields will fall if energy prices drop, but investors will continue to be driven by the economics and the Government’s willingness to take tough fiscal decisions, both of which point to yields staying high.”

UK borrowing costs are growing amid a wider bond market sell-off after Donald Trump rejected a peace deal with Iran over the weekend, pushing oil prices higher.

Brent crude, the international benchmark, rose by 3pc to just over $108 a barrel on Monday, adding to global inflation pressures. Bond traders reacted by demanding higher yields from governments to lend them money.

The yield on 10-year US Treasury bonds rose to above 5.24pc, the highest level since 2007.

News.title: Taylor Swift becomes most-awarded artist in MTV history
News.content:
Taylor Swift broke records at the 2026 MTV Video Music Awards (VMAs) on Sunday, becoming the most-awarded artist in VMA history.

The pop star, 36, was previously tied with Beyoncé for the title, with 30 VMAs each. However, Swift took home three awards at the ceremony, bringing her career total to an unmatched 33.

The Fate of Ophelia, ⁠Swift’s first single from her record-breaking The Life of a Showgirl album, claimed the top trophy – Video of the Year – and she dedicated the honour to the late country music legend Dolly Parton.

During her speech, Swift praised Parton as “the ultimate showgirl” who told stories that were “so vivid and so rich”.

“I think that we were all very lucky to share this planet with Dolly Parton for a time,” she said.

Parton, an award-winning country singer, died in August at the age of 80.

Swift also received the inaugural Artist Director Honors, a new award meant to recognise artists “whose work behind the camera has expanded the possibilities of music video and advanced the art of visual storytelling”.

The 36-year-old has written and directed 18 videos of her roughly 60 videos during her career. The ‌most recent, for ‌her new single Patient Zero, debuted during ⁠the ceremony.

News.title: Five reasons why Australia’s win over Boks was an all-time classic
News.content:
If the Wallabies play like this in their own backyard at their own World Cup next year, boy we are in for a treat. After years in the doldrums, this five-try victory over South Africa was the latest reminder of their transformation under the stewardship of Les Kiss.

Their gritty performance in Perth – the city where Australia will open rugby’s showpiece in 12 months’ time – was caveated by the fact they were facing a second-string Boks side. But there can be no denying they are on an upward trajectory, even if their discipline dramatically deserted them late on.

In a helter-skelter denouement, Australia played the majority of the final 10 minutes of the match with 11 men on the pitch as South Africa threatened to mount a late comeback. Tom Wright’s eye-catching intercept try looked to have secured a match-winning moment, but it was scratched off after Hunter Paisami joined Harry Wilson, Ryan Lonergan and Joseph Sua’ali’i in the bin.

Ox Nche’s 80th-minute score made it a four-point game with time left for the restart, but Australia had enough fight to secure a dramatic victory largely built on execution and patience.

Five tries by the hour mark, including a Len Ikitau first-half double, ultimately gave South Africa a mountain to climb. The Wallabies’ field coverage and industriousness in defence was far superior to that of the four-time world champions, while Max Jorgensen and Sua’ali’i were pillars of excellence out wide.

After clinching a 3-1 win over New Zealand in their historic “Greatest Rivalry” series, Rassie Erasmus had the luxury of resting several of his A-listers for this one-off Test in Western Australia. The changes ultimately had an adverse effect, with the visitors faulty at the set-piece and lacking their usual snarl and bite. They found themselves playing catch-up in a chaotic game that Australia, despite their discipline creaking in the dying moments, deserved to win.

Here, Telegraph Sport explores five reasons why this was one of the craziest Test matches in recent memory.

Wallabies outmuscle Boks over 60 emphatic minutes

The Wallabies front up impressively to earn a seven-point lead at the break after a quickfire Len Ikitau double cancels out tries from Johan Grobbelaar and Edwill van der Merwe, before Ben Donaldson finishes a sublime attacking set from the hosts.

News.title: England show ODI depth in thrashing of Sri Lanka
News.content:
England’s international summer comes to an end at the Oval with a series decider against Sri Lanka. After England won the first game in Durham, Sri Lanka bounced back to take a 16-run win at Headingley on Thursday to set up this winner-takes-all match today. Sri Lanka put up a much better fight in the second one-day international than they have throughout the rest of their white-ball tour. The tourists posted 321 for six, with their captain Kusal Mendis leading the way with 121 off 100 balls, his seventh ODI century.

England’s reply got off to the best possible start, with both openers Tom Banton and Ben Duckett hitting fifties. It appeared to be going well for England, with Jos Buttler and Will Jacks also registering half centuries, but Buttler’s hamstring injury in addition to the regular loss of wickets meant Sri Lanka were able to claim victory to take us to a series decider in London today.

“I am so happy winning and getting the hundred,” Mendis said. “The overall performance was very good. We started really well and the middle order batted really well. Nothing special, basic cricket and I was very happy with 320, we wanted more than 300 on this pitch. [Dunith] Wellalage bowled really well, the whole team, after the powerplay. The guys gave 100 per cent. Today [Thursday] is finished and now we have to focus on the next game and do the basics right.”

When Buttler retired hurt in the 38th over of England’s run chase, the hosts were 254 for four and were in a great position to chase the total down and claim a series victory. From the 37th over onwards, England were only able to score one four and one six.

“It was an outstanding game,” England captain Harry Brook said. “You can look back and dwell on some many different areas but that is not what this team does, we go back to the drawing board and get ready for the Oval. We put up a really good fight with the ball. To restrict them to 320 and have the chance to chase that down was a hell of an effort.

“The lads got the chase off to a flyer. You could not really ask for much more. We probably stalled in that middle period and lost a few too many wickets, but the fight we showed was great. We have got a great opportunity now to try and win this series, and a great opportunity for 12 months’ time. In pressure situations, like the one that awaits us at the Oval, it will be great to see where we are as a team.”

Buttler has been ruled out of this match due to a hamstring injury and has been replaced in the squad by Dan Lawrence, who had been playing for Surrey in the final round of the County Championship.

Play from the Oval will get under way at 10.30am.

News.title: Saracens storm Leicester to launch new Venter era in style

Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of this mouthwatering Gallagher Prem meeting as Leicester Tigers host Saracens at Welford Road.

“Firstly we are looking to evolve our game, we’re not looking to rip it up and completely restart,” he said. For me it’s all about being consistently near the top and then getting in those big games and having the ability to perform in them.”

“I’m well aware that there’s lots of elements from the season and different circumstances but the main thing is that the league is designed to have a top four that go into the play-offs so the top four is the aim.”

Saracens finished one place below Leicester in the previous campaign and missed out on the play-offs after a 32-12 final round loss to Exeter Chiefs.

Boss Joe Shaw has handed debuts to Tomos Williams and Alfie Barbeary, and he’s raring to go ahead of this fixture.

“We’ve had a great pre-season, but we’re itching to get stuck into the league campaign now,” he said. “We have a really competitive squad who are driving standards and good habits across the pitch. We are confident in the squad we have put together and are excited to see what they can achieve this campaign.”

The Premier League finally broke their silence and released a statement alleging Man City had been found guilty of “ALL charges related to serious breaches” of their financial rules.

Harris quoted the Prem’s statement that revealed City arranged “sham” commercial deals with sponsors.

Why isn’t Granit Xhaka playing for Switzerland against Scotland?

Granit Xhaka pulled out of the Switzerland squad after admitting to receiving a fake Covid-19 vaccination certificate during the pandemic.

The Sunderland midfielder withdrew amid a criminal investigation from the public prosecutor’s office in the Swiss city of Lucerne.

The controversy came to light amid suspicions that a female doctor in Lucerne issued vaccination certificates without ever administering the jabs.

The doctor has denied allegations. However, a statement on Xhaka’s Instagram admitted his guilt.



The statement read: “In recent days, a lot has been reported about an issue from my past. I would like to address it personally.

“At the time, in connection with the Covid-19 vaccination, I was personally very uncertain and had serious concerns. I had deep distrust of the vaccine and was affected by fear and uncertainty.

“In this emotionally charged situation, I obtained a vaccination certificate instead of having my unanswered questions clarified through the proper channels.

“Today, I clearly see that this was not the right course of action. It was a mistake. I am sorry.



“I take responsibility for the decision, will face the process of clarifying the facts, and will cooperate fully with the relevant authorities.”

Xhaka was still an Arsenal player during the pandemic. He left North London to sign for German club Bayer Leverkusen in 2023 before returning to England with Sunderland in 2025.

A spokesperson for the Lucerne Cantonal Prosecutor’s Office said: “The aim is to clarify whether there has been conduct relevant under criminal law in connection with the possible fraudulent obtaining of a false certification and/or document forgery.”

While there was never a legal requirement to obtain or hold such a certificate, the Swiss office of public health confirmed it was needed for access to various activities, venues and travel. That meant that participation was restricted for anyone who did not possess one.



The measures were in place in Switzerland until the spring of 2022. Covid-19 certificates were still issued after that point, primarily to enable residents to meet entry requirements to foreign countries when travelling.

Swiss cops raided the doctor’s clinic in 2023 and seized evidence as part of investigations involving a number of people believed to have obtained coronavirus certificates.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

According to reports in his homeland, the investigations centre on whether Xhaka secured a certificate proving he had received the vaccine despite never actually being vaccinated.

The public prosecutor’s office has confirmed an investigation is underway.

When asked if he was struggling with boredom at the EFC General Assembly in Copenhagen, Schmeichel replied: “Beyond belief.

“Because I didn’t retire on my own terms, I still have my competitive edge.

“I would like to manage – to be a football manager or higher. The fire is still burning quite strongly.

“I don’t really enjoy getting the [coaching] badges, but you have got to get them. When I am on the pitch – coaching or helping youngsters coming through – I do get enjoyment out of that.

Speaking about his son’s situation, he added: “It is a difficult period for Kasper now. One day you are somebody. You have an identity. And then the next day you have nothing.

Sports.title: Shameless Man City cheated us all - Prem titles are now worthless and must be stripped
Sports.content:
Shameless Man City cheated us all - Prem titles are now worthless and must be stripped

The Premier League's statement condemning Manchester City following the investigation into the 115 charges against them is so damning surely there is no way back for the club's current ownership

View 2 Images Manchester City have been found guilty by the independent commission following their legal battle with the Premier League. (Image: PA Wire)

In black and white, it takes your breath away.

‌



The words look more from a White House political scandal rather than football. The most telling words of all: “The £900m sham.” The Premier League’s statement was not just damning - it absolutely torched Manchester City.

‌



The sheer scale of sham contracts, false accounting, cover-ups, lying witnesses and deception is mind-blowing. This is fraud on an industrial scale. The 40 page document spelling out the verdict, the case and the evidence which brought the 115 charges is an astonishing read in itself.

‌



The Premier League has bared its teeth - and they have been absolutely brutal in their summing up. They have taken their time - but this absolutely destroys Manchester City.

‌



It attacks Project Longbow. It even attacks the ownership and Abu Dhabi state-owned companies and sponsorship. State ownership is now allowed - and so this part could have wider ramifications. The 40 page document is staggering in its detail and accusations.

It destroys the club’s reputation, mocks its protestations and makes it clear enough is enough.

City have until Friday to appeal - and then an appeal board will be set up to resolve the case “as soon as possible.” The reality is that their defiant counter statement - which says the club is still in denial - makes it clear they will appeal. So, we will have to wait longer for an outcome.

‌



But the Premier League has been accused of a slow process, dragging football through the mud by taking too long and getting tied down by lawyers. And yet now, by comparison, they are going at a turbo-charged pace. They have given City just days to appeal.

It feels obvious why: they are determined to make them pay and hit them with the hardest punishment possible.

This case could bring down City as a football club as we know it, its owners and the language used makes it feel impossible for them to continue in the Premier League under this ownership.

‌



It is that severe. It is that damning. It is hard to know how City pick themselves up and go again under the Abu Dhabi ownership.

View 2 Images Khaldoon Al Mubarak and Ferran Soriano have both responded defiantly to the verdict (Image: Getty Images)

The statement talks about “sham” contracts and “sham” agreements with others, to artificially inflate the club’s revenues and reduce its costs. The club filed misstated accounts and “concealed” the true state of its finances from auditors and football regulators. And it says “Manchester City was significantly in breach of both the Premier League’s and UEFA’s spending limits” before saying the club misled the investigation.

‌



How on earth does a club come back from that? How does an ownership come back from that? Answer is you cannot.

City have to be relegated. That must come with a points deduction and a severe punishment to ensure that this goes just one season on the naughty step. We are talking nine years of deception from 2009 to 2018 and the punishment has to reflect that.

Premier League chief executive Richard Masters said: “It also vindicates the Premier League’s decision to pursue this case against Manchester City.

‌



“While the process to date has been both long and difficult, the League has remained determined that the facts be established independently.”

He is right. Yes, it has taken too long. But they had to get the investigation and process right. Now the Premier League has been vindicated. They have to throw the book at City - and make sure there is no way back. They have cheated us all. They have cheated their way to trophies and success.

I have not been in favor of stripping titles - and this verdict and the document and detail has changed my mind. It goes beyond titles having an asterisk. They are now worthless.

Sports.title: Man City chief's secret message to staff after bombshell Premier League verdict emerges
Sports.content:
Man City chief's secret message to staff after bombshell Premier League verdict emerges

Manchester City have been found guilty of the Premier League charges and the eight-time champions have now hit out at the allegations ahead of a possible appeal over the coming days

View 2 Images Khaldoon Al Mubarak and Ferran Soriano (Image: Getty Images)

Manchester City's chief executive, Ferran Soriano, has sent a video message to staff members claiming that the club will continue fighting their guilty verdict.

The Premier League confirmed on Tuesday that the club had been found guilty of all charges, with the process now moving towards an appeal. That is an avenue that City will take advantage of. Before that, CEO of the City Football Group Foriano has got in touch with club employees.

He sent a three minute video message, obtained by the Manchester Evening News, to staff members and said that they will continue attempting to clear their name and suggested that the Premier League's verdict is based on a 'single false accusation'.

‌



"I want to share some information related to the ongoing disciplinary process between Manchester City and the Premier League. A document has been made public with an opinion of the Premier League commission that is negative to our interests. I want to explain exactly what this is, the next steps and how we are going to continue to defend the club, and finally be vindicated in this process.

‌



"This has gone for so long that it is important to remind ourselves that the whole Premier League case against us is based on a single false accusation - that the owners' personal money was somehow and secretly put into the club via some sponsors from Abu Dhabi. This is just not true.

"Irrefutable evidence has been provided to the Premier League commission that shows that it could not happen and that it did not happen. This includes bank statements, money transfers, witnesses and everything necessary to categorically demonstrate that the money did not come from the owner. Every other false charge that has been thrown at us - and aggressively marketed and promoted - comes from the simple, central, and completely false accusation.

"Surprisingly for us, and for our lawyers, after nearly two years the Premier League Commission has introduced an opinion that supports the Premier League's conspiracy theory. To do so, the opinion had to ignore the extensive evidence provided by the club in order to reach a conclusion that is clearly wrong.

‌



View 2 Images Ferran Soriano has sent a message to Man City employees (Image: Getty Images)

"Our lawyers will now file an appeal that sets out the opinion contains clear material errors of law, principle and fact and it is unsafe. Remember we have been here before. In 2020 we were also wrongly ruled against for many of the same issues. We appealed to an independent body in CAS and we won.

"We will now be relentless in our work. We will focus on the independent appeal process and also all other legal avenues available to us in order to win the case, and we will take all necessary action to protect the club and seek compensation from any party that tries to damage it now, and in the future.

‌



"I know this can be a bit of a distraction but please remain focused on our business and take care of our extended City family as we always do. Please follow the normal protocols in referring to fan, partner and media enquiries. Very soon we will look back at this and recognise it is another time in our history when we dealt with adversity and overcame it together."

Soriano's message comes in the aftermath of a strong statement from City in response to the Premier League's verdict. It read: "Manchester City FC is both disappointed and surprised by the opinion of the Premier League Commission, that has been published today.

Man City 115 charges delay explained as commission lay out Premier League timeline READ MORE :

"The Club is innocent of the accusations made by the Premier League and a comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence exists in support of all of its positions, relating to this case. The Club will therefore be relentless, and where necessary proactive, in any and all appropriate regulatory and legal forums.

‌



"The Premier League process remains ongoing, with significant elements uncompleted. Manchester City FC will now pursue the appeal avenues open to it, on the basis that the opinion contains clear material errors, of law, principle and fact, and is unsafe.

"The Club has diligently respected due process for eight years on the basis that the Premier League Board and Executive would behave as an independent, impartial and fair-minded regulator, free from partisan influence. The Club is obviously restricted in what it can say further until all future proceedings are complete."

Elsewhere, Premier League CEO Richard Masters has claimed that the Premier League are attempting to wrap up the proceedings as soon as possible. In a statement, he said:“The core decision establishes the facts of what happened at Manchester City during this period. It details how the club systematically broke Premier League Rules for nearly a decade.

‌



“It also vindicates the Premier League’s decision to pursue this case against Manchester City. While the process to date has been both long and difficult, the League has remained determined that the facts be established independently.

“It is a key responsibility of the Premier League to ensure that the Rules, approved by the clubs themselves, are upheld to protect the integrity of the competition. It is paramount that the League remains competitive and fair for all clubs and for the fans. We take that role extremely seriously.

“This disciplinary case, and this decision, are the most significant in Premier League history. There are elements of the case that remain to be decided, including, importantly, what sanction must follow for these breaches. Now we have the Commission’s decision, we are committed to moving swiftly through the remainder of the process, to provide certainty for the League, our clubs and fans.”

Sports.title: Man City 115 charges delay explained as commission lay out Premier League timeline
Sports.content:
Man City 115 charges delay explained as commission lay out Premier League timeline

Manchester City have been found guilty by the independent commission who have now explained the reason behind the delay

View 3 Images Manchester City have been found guilty by the independent commission following their legal battle with the Premier League. (Image: PA Wire)

The independent Commission has explained the reason behind the 20-month delay following the end of the 42-day hearing into the Premier League and Manchester City's 115 charges. The investigation into Man City began in December 2018, and a complaint was subsequently issued under Section W of the League’s rules in February 2023.

‌



The Premier League announced in a statement today (Wednesday) that City were found guilty of 'all charges related to serious breaches of the Premier League’s financial rules over a nine-season period, and the majority of charges in relation to its failure to co-operate with the League’s investigation.' The club still maintain their innocence.

‌



In a statement, the independent Commission explained the reason behind the lengthy delay and wrote: "It has taken us much longer than we would have wished, and much longer than we had anticipated would be the case when the hearing concluded, to produce our Decision. That is regrettable.

‌



FOLLOW OUR MAN CITY FB PAGE! Follow our Manchester City Mirror Football Facebook page

"However, we were fortunate to have available to us throughout the period in which our Decision has been being prepared not only all of the documents that were used at the hearing but also (a) verbatim transcripts of the evidence given by each witness and expert at the hearing.

"Those transcripts ran to approximately 7,000 pages, and (b) extremely detailed written submissions from the parties (that they had supplemented orally over four days at the end of the hearing) on the evidence and each of the numerous issues that we were tasked with determining in the proceedings."

‌



Premier League chief executive Richard Masters also broke his silence on the investigation and said: "The core decision establishes the facts of what happened at Manchester City during this period. It details how the club systematically broke Premier League Rules for nearly a decade.

View 3 Images Richard Masters, CEO of the Premier League, has released a statement on Manchester City's rule breaches. (Image: PA Wire)

"It also vindicates the Premier League’s decision to pursue this case against Manchester City. While the process to date has been both long and difficult, the League has remained determined that the facts be established independently.

‌



"It is a key responsibility of the Premier League to ensure that the Rules, approved by the clubs themselves, are upheld to protect the integrity of the competition. It is paramount that the League remains competitive and fair for all clubs and for the fans. We take that role extremely seriously.

"This disciplinary case, and this decision, are the most significant in Premier League history. There are elements of the case that remain to be decided, including, importantly, what sanction must follow for these breaches.

"Now we have the Commission’s decision, we are committed to moving swiftly through the remainder of the process, to provide certainty for the League, our clubs and fans."

‌



View 3 Images City have been found guilty (Image: Getty Images)

City however, maintain their innocence and have until the end of this week, Friday, October 3 to lodge and appeal. They released a statement which read: "Manchester City FC is both disappointed and surprised by the opinion of the Premier League Commission, which has been published today.

"The Club is innocent of the accusations made by the Premier League and a comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence exists in support of all of its positions, relating to this case. The Club will therefore be relentless, and where necessary proactive, in any and all appropriate regulatory and legal forums.

Article continues below

"The Premier League process remains ongoing, with significant elements uncompleted. Manchester City FC will now pursue the appeal avenues open to it, on the basis that the opinion contains clear material errors, of law, principle and fact, and is unsafe.

"The Club has diligently respected due process for eight years on the basis that the Premier League Board and Executive would behave as an independent, impartial and fair-minded regulator, free from partisan influence.

"The Club is obviously restricted in what it can say further until all future proceedings are complete."

Sports.title: Man Utd given Bruno Fernandes injury update as Michael Carrick given fresh headache
Sports.content:
Man Utd given Bruno Fernandes injury update as Michael Carrick given fresh headache

Bruno Fernandes missed Portugal’s clash with Norway last week after a persistent issue but the playmaker now appears set to return to contention for his nation ahead of their next game

View 2 Images Bruno Fernandes could play for Portugal on Thursday (Image: Getty Images)

Manchester United have been handed a huge Bruno Fernandes boost, with the midfielder now fully fit. The Red Devils initially had a concern after Fernandes had missed Portugal’s clash with Norway last week.

‌



He had been undergoing an individual training programme and remained on international duty. And it now appears that Fernandes has now returned to full fitness.

‌



According to reports in Portugal, the 32-year-old travelled to Malmo with the rest of his teammates and took part in training as normal. It is suggested that there were no lasting effects and Fernandes is now considered available for his nation’s clash with Denmark in Copenhagen.

‌



Of course, United will be delighted that he has not sustained a long-term issue but might have preferred more recovery time for their captain. Instead, it is being suggested that he could be restored to Portugal’s starting XI.

"The club has the right to appeal the independent Commission’s findings and has until Friday 2 October to exercise that right. The Premier League Board’s intention is that the full process (including any appeals and publication of relevant decisions) is concluded as soon as possible."

Sports.title: 'Sham' deals and 'dishonest' witnesses - key revelations from Man City verdict
Sports.content:
In a damning 40-page document, an independent commission laid bare its findings into Manchester City's breaches of the Premier League's financial rules. Here, Sky Sports takes a look at the key revelations...

Guilty on all serious financial charges

Manchester City were found guilty of all charges related to serious breaches of Premier League financial rules between the 2009-10 and 2017-18 seasons.

The charge that was not proven was regarding one element of the Premier League's non-cooperation case.

'Disguised funding scheme'

The independent commission repeatedly concluded that a number of City's commercial agreements were "shams".

City used a "disguised funding scheme" where Abu Dhabi United Group (ADUG) partially funded sponsorship fees. This allowed the club to avoid breaking the record for the largest single-season loss in Premier League history.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports News takes you through a timeline of Manchester City's charge

Sponsorship inflated by more than £830m

The club filed accounts that the commission found concealed the true nature of their finances from auditors and football regulators.

City overstated their sponsorship income by £830.69m with agreements that were "far in excess" of fair market value.

The commission concluded that City's financial statements for the seasons between 2009-10 and 2017-18 "did not show a true and fair view" of the club's financial position.

The commission found three separate remuneration agreements that were omitted from City's accounts and paid by ADUG.

'The Fordham Arrangement'

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports News has obtained a video of Man City CEO Ferran Soriano that was sent to internal staff and players at the club after the guilty verdict in relation to allegations of serious breaches of financial rules

City used a third party, Fordham, as a device to overstate income by £24.5m and understate expenses by £49.414m.

The commission described 'The Fordham Arrangement' as being "little more than a front for ADUG".

The Fordham Arrangement was, the commission contended, "a further device by which ADUG funds could be paid into the club in a manner that concealed their true origin" and which enabled "the club to remove operating expenses from its financial statements".

The Fordham Arrangement was part of a system called 'Project Longbow' which "was a multi-strand project whose purpose was to explore how the club might boost its revenues and reduce its operating losses".

But while "many of the strands of Project Longbow were genuine, legitimate attempts to achieve those aims. One was not. That was the Fordham Arrangement".

'Dishonest witnesses'

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports News' Kaveh Solhekol explains what Man City's penalty could be and when a decision will be made

The independent commission heard factual evidence from 27 witnesses over 42 days in the last quarter of 2024, with a core bundle of key documents running to "many tens of thousands of pages".

The commission says the club made concerted efforts to stop and frustrate the investigation.

It also found some witnesses on behalf of the club gave false evidence, while other City witnesses were found by the commission to give knowingly untrue evidence and so had been dishonest.

City 'intended to circumvent PL rules'

The commission found City had breached UEFA and Premier League financial rules, while also ruling that "by its conduct the club clearly intended to circumvent the PL rules".

The Premier League said it regarded City's conduct as having "extremely serious, significant, sustained and intentional or reckless breaches of rules critical to the proper and fair operation of the Premier League's league competition".

Manchester City have confirmed they will appeal against the ruling and have until Friday October 2 to do so.

Sports.title: Fitzpatrick's 'best period of golf' ever? | 'I've contended a lot!'

Matt Fitzpatrick believes he is currently playing the best golf of his career, ahead of the world No 4 teeing it up alongside his father at the Alfred Dunhill Links Championship.

Fitzpatrick registered a fourth worldwide win of the season with a three-shot victory at the FedEx Open de France on Sunday, having already won three times on the PGA Tour during an impressive campaign.

The Englishman failed to finish higher than 14th in any of the majors in 2026 but still had six worldwide top 10s along with his victories, with Fitzpatrick proud of his season and contending so frequently.

"This is the best period of golf I've played for sure," Fitzpatrick told the Sky Sports Golf podcast. "2022 was right up there, but I've had three wins and obviously a fourth now. I think just the sustained consistency has been the big thing really.

"Obviously that [a disappointing major season] is a disappointment. It's the goal of anyone's at the start of the year to contend in the majors - those are what mean the most and those are what matter.

Sports.title: Buttler: McCullum can go 'all in' on Cricket World Cup without Test role
Sports.content:
Jos Buttler believes Brendon McCullum's removal as Test coach may have boosted England's World Cup chances, with the New Zealander now "all in" on lifting the trophy next winter.

McCullum was relieved of his red-ball duties in July, with Stephen Fleming eventually named as his successor, but remained in charge of a limited-overs set-up that ended the summer with a record of 11 wins and two defeats.

That included ODI series wins over India and Sri Lanka, raising England's stock in a format that has seen them decline since they became world champions in 2019.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player McCullum has remained in charge of England's white-ball teams, alongside specialist mentor Kevin Pietersen

Buttler, who captained the team in their ill-fated 2023 title defence, thinks the split coaching model has allowed McCullum to throw all his energy towards next year's tournament in southern Africa.

"He's only got one focus now and that is the white ball," Buttler said on his For the Love of Cricket podcast.

"It's not that he couldn't do everything, because he could, but your time is more spread and you've got more to think about with the Test team as well.

"Now he can focus solely on white-ball cricket - T20, yes, but mainly ODI cricket with that World Cup on the horizon. It seems like Baz is naturally all in on, 'how do I win this World Cup with this team?'

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Buttler said McCullum now has more time to focus on the white-ball format

"I think he can sort of see that World Cup is not that far away. It's a real target, now his remit has changed from four months ago being in charge of everything to, 'right, I can really nail down on this'. He's just got more time and more focus on that.

"ODI cricket for England has not been consistently great for a couple of years, so there's some nice growth to go on that and this summer's been a really good start."

Buttler delivers update on hamstring injury

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Buttler was forced to retire after suffering a hamstring injury during England's second ODI against Sri Lanka

Buttler is currently sidelined with a hamstring injury and has already been ruled out for the forthcoming tri-series tour of Pakistan.

He is also a doubt for the November trip to Australia, meaning the team's most experienced one-day player could miss as many as eight ODIs and a significant chunk of the pre-World Cup preparations.

"I've had a scan and I'm waiting to see the specialist. Then we'll know what the next steps are," he said.

"The unknown is often the tough part. Any cricketer just wants a physio or a doctor to tell you, 'on this date you'll be back playing cricket'. Unfortunately, they can't do that just yet."

Sports.title: Manchester City guilty over Premier League charges after £900m of ‘sham’ contracts
Sports.content:
The Premier League has confirmed Manchester City have been found guilty of all charges of breaching its financial rules over a nine-year period, with the club found to have boosted their income by a staggering amount of more than £900m.

In a bombshell announcement the Premier League revealed an independent commission had found City guilty of arranging “sham contracts” with commercial partners to artificially inflate revenues and reduce costs, and of filing inaccurate accounts to hide the true state of their finances, which if accurately reported would have led to significant breaches of Premier League and Uefa spending limits.

The club were also found to have entered into “sham” image rights deals with players and the then manager Roberto Mancini to artificially inflate their earnings.

City have said they will appeal by Friday’s deadline “on the basis that the opinion contains clear material errors, of law, principle and fact, and is unsafe”. Their chief executive, Ferran Soriano, said in a video to employees that the decision was based on a “Premier League conspiracy theory”.

The appeal is expected to run aside a sanctions hearing presided over by the independent commission, with the Premier League eager to conclude matters as quickly as possible.

The extraordinary scale of what Hull’s owner, Acun Ilicali, has described as City’s “financial doping” has sent shock waves throughout the world of football, leaving executives at other Premier League clubs stunned.

The Premier League’s chief executive, Richard Masters, described the case “as the most significant in Premier League history”. It seems inevitable it will lead to an unprecedented punishment, including in all probability a points deduction that will condemn City to relegation.

Although there is no direct precedent given the scale of City’s offences, Everton’s 10-point penalty for breaching profitability and sustainability rules by £19.5m over a period ending with the 2021-22 season was based on a Premier League tariff of six points for the initial breach, plus an additional point for every £5m the club overspent.

The commission made damning comments regarding the behaviour of City witnesses during the hearings. “Evidence given by a number of important factual witnesses called to give evidence on behalf of the club was false in a number of key respects,” it wrote, arguing that some witnesses had given evidence “they knew to be untrue and so had been dishonest”.

City were found to have operated a “disguised funding scheme” worth £830.6m over nine seasons, from 2009-10 to 2017-18, and to have hidden costs by a further £70m. In addition the club have been found guilty of multiple breaches of failing to cooperate with the Premier League and act in good faith. The commission concluded the club had made concerted efforts to stop and frustrate the investigation.

The Premier League published a redacted 40-page “core decision” from the independent commission, which has taken almost two years to produce after a 42-day hearing that concluded in December 2024.

The league said: “The independent commission found City arranged ‘sham’ commercial deals with a number of its sponsors during the period, which were part of a disguised funding scheme, whereby those companies were only required to pay a portion of the relevant sponsorship fees. The remainder was funded by Abu Dhabi United Group Investment & Development Ltd (ADUG), which owned the club.

View image in fullscreen Manchester City chief executive Ferran Soriano leaving the European Football Clubs board meeting in Copenhagen. Photograph: PA Video/PA

“As part of the scheme, further ‘sham’ arrangements, funded by ADUG, were entered into to enable the club to record lower operating expenses than it actually incurred, as well as a ‘sham’ circular arrangement with Fordham, an entity that purchased the club’s players’ image rights, that was funded by ADUG.

“The purpose of these schemes was found to have been to artificially inflate the club’s revenues, and reduce its costs, by more than £900m during the affected period, to appear to comply with financial rules.

“The consequence of this, as the commission found, was that the club filed misstated accounts and concealed the true state of its finances from its auditors and football regulators.”

ADUG bought City on behalf of Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed al-Nahyan for £200m in 2008, with the new owners making an immediate impact by paying £32.5m to sign the Brazilian superstar Robinho from Real Madrid. That was the start of a spending spree City struggled to afford from their existing revenues, with the independent commission concluding that the only way to match the owners’ ambitions for the club was for ADUG to “provide very significant funds by way of equity contribution”.

Quick Guide How do I 

The commission report states that in 2010 City devised a scheme whereby sponsors would pay a “base sum” and ADUG would pay a “tagged sum”, despite the base sum being the only true revenue. The recorded sponsorship fee would be the total of them both.

City’s lawyers claimed that the “tagged sum” was a loan by the Abu Dhabi government on liabilities on sponsorship fees. The commission rejected that argument.

The judgment is a huge victory for the Premier League and Masters. Despite the commission demonstrating that City breached Uefa’s spending limits there appears little prospect of Uefa’s case being revisited because there is a five-year statute of limitations on its disciplinary proceedings. Uefa’s punishment of City in relation to alleged financial fair play breaches was largely overturned in 2020 by the court of arbitration for sport, which found “most of the alleged breaches were either not established or time-barred”.

Masters said: “The core decision establishes the facts of what happened at Manchester City during this period. It details how the club systematically broke Premier League rules for nearly a decade. It also vindicates the Premier League’s decision to pursue this case against Manchester City.”

He said in relation to sanctions: “Now we have the commission’s decision, we are committed to moving swiftly through the remainder of the process, to provide certainty for the league, our clubs and fans.”

Other Premier League clubs are surprised City have not reached an agreed sanction with the Premier League, given the judgment, but City continue to deny wrongdoing. “Manchester City FC is both disappointed and surprised by the opinion of the Premier League commission, that has been published today,” the club said. “The club is innocent of the accusations made by the Premier League and a comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence exists in support of all of its positions, relating to this case. The club will therefore be relentless, and where necessary proactive, in any and all appropriate regulatory and legal forums.”

Sports.title: ‘The emperor is naked’: Uefa president Ceferin takes new swipe at Infantino
Sports.content:
The Uefa president, Aleksander Ceferin, has attacked his embattled Fifa counterpart Gianni Infantino in a scathing takedown of the failed Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) project and other recent scandals, saying “the emperor is naked” and declaring “it is time to say ‘enough’”.

In a pointed address to the European Football Clubs (EFC) general assembly, Ceferin did not mention Infantino by name but made clear his view that Fifa’s leadership must change. He drew on the event’s location, Copenhagen, to make a comparison to Hans Christian Andersen’s The Emperor’s New Clothes in assessing Infantino’s conduct, making clear reference to the peace prize awarded to Donald Trump and last summer’s Folarin Balogun affair along with the FFE scheme.

“An emperor is persuaded that he is wearing magnificent clothes – clothes which, he is told, only the foolish or unfit cannot see,” Ceferin said. “His court goes along with it. Until a child simply says aloud what everyone can see: the emperor is naked. Perhaps the moral of the story is this: convenient words cannot change uncomfortable realities.

“Selling part of football’s future does not become development because you call it development. Putting a fait accompli in front of national associations does not become democratisation because you call it democratisation, however big the cheque is. And secrecy does not become consultation because you call it consultation.”

Ceferin suggested to the ­hundreds of club representatives present that ­Infantino’s behaviour would not be tolerated at one of their organisations. “Imagine one of your senior executives secretly negotiating away control of your club’s crown jewels,” he said. “You didn’t know. Your board didn’t know. Your players and fans didn’t know. And by the time you find out, the deal is almost done. What would your board do?

“Imagine that he creates a peace prize for a political leader, without his own board having any say over its creation or its recipient. Then, that same political leader calls during the biggest competition in the world to complain about a decision on the pitch. The rules say one thing. The phone rings. Then the decision changes.

“How many times would this have to happen at your club before the board says: ‘enough’? I think it is time to say ‘enough’. No office, no title and no amount of power gives anyone the right to sell the future of football.”

The ongoing war of words between football’s biggest governing bodies had already intensified on Tuesday when Fifa accused Uefa of waging a “misinformation campaign” and trying to influence the race for its presidency, urging a US court to reject Uefa’s request to receive documents for use in a planned criminal complaint against Infantino.

Senior figures within Uefa remain adamant that a candidate to oppose Infantino in the Fifa election next March must be found before the 18 November deadline for nominations. The EFC chair, Nasser al-Khelaifi, has been mooted in the past as a future contender but conclusively ruled himself out of the Fifa presidency in the Danish capital.

“I have zero interest in Fifa, zero agenda or ambition to be there,” al-Khelaifi said. “I don’t think I’m the right guy for this position. I’m enjoying what I’m doing, having fun. Fifa, not for me.”

Al-Khelaifi has designs on expanding the scope of his own organisation. In his speech to the general assembly he said “now is the time to create World Football Clubs”, explicitly stating that a representative body including those beyond Europe should be formed. “We are more than proud and happy if we can help and contribute outside of Europe for our colleagues from different clubs in the world,” he said later.

Sports.title: Chloe Kelly and Ella Toone dropped by England after not hitting ‘expected’ level
Sports.content:
Ella Toone and Chloe Kelly have been dropped from England’s squad because of their performance levels by Sarina Wiegman, who has given a first call-up to the 20-year-old ­Chelsea midfielder Lexi Potter.

Toone and Kelly have played key roles in England’s run of three consecutive major tournament finals but Wiegman made clear on Tuesday, when announcing her selection for the Women’s World Cup qualifying playoff against Greece, that she wants to see more from them for their clubs.

“The main reason is that I think the levels weren’t what I expect from them on the pitch,” Wiegman said. The head coach “still believes in them” but said: “We expect a bit more and we know they can bring more. That was the message.

“There is also competition going on. It’s about talent, it’s about playing minutes and it’s about the ­competition going on. I hope they can step up and show what they can do.

Quick Guide England squad Show Goalkeepers: Hannah Hampton (Chelsea), Khiara Keating (Liverpool), Anna Moorhouse (Manchester City on loan from Orlando Pride) Defenders: Lucy Bronze (Chelsea), Jess Carter (Gotham), Niamh Charles (Manchester City), Grace Fisk (Liverpool), Alex Greenwood (Manchester City), Maya Le Tissier (Manchester United), Esme Morgan (Washington Spirit), Leah Williamson (Arsenal) Midfielders: Laura Blindkilde Brown (Manchester City), Lucia Kendall (Aston Villa), Erica Meg Parkinson (North Carolina Courage), Lexi Potter (Chelsea), Georgia Stanway (Arsenal), Keira Walsh (Chelsea) Forwards: Freya Godfrey (London City Lionesses), Lauren Hemp (Manchester City), Lauren James (Chelsea), Beth Mead (Manchester City), Jess Park (Manchester United), Alessia Russo (Arsenal) Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

“I’m convinced they can do better, I think they are convinced about that, too. I think they took the feedback in a good and in a positive way but it’s hard to take at the same time of course; it’s not a nice message. I hope they respond to it really well. We will support them and of course they get the support at club, too. I hope they come back even better than they were before.”

Neither Toone nor Kelly has scored or provided an assist in the Women’s Super League this season, although Toone did score in ­Manchester United’s 10-1 League Cup victory against the second-tier side ­Sheffield United last week, after she had been left out of their draw at Arsenal. Toone has started three of United’s four WSL games. Kelly has started one of Arsenal’s league matches, their ­Champions League win against Køge and made three WSL substitute appearances.

There was also no place for the Chelsea forward Aggie Beever‑Jones. Wiegman has called up the uncapped 18-year-old midfielder Erica Meg ­Parkinson and the London City Lionesses winger Freya Godfrey, and there is a return after injury for the captain, Leah Williamson.

There had been growing calls for the inclusion of Potter this term after her strong form for Chelsea, ­including her starring role in the 1-0 victory against Arsenal on Sunday. “She’s grown a lot,” Wiegman said.

“Last season we kept a close eye on her because she was getting into the squad and playing really well. But I think she’s started the season so well. Her performances have really impressed us so she really deserves this call-up.

“She’s shown at Chelsea that she can start against any team. The last game I thought she did very well against a top Arsenal [team]. What I’ve seen from her is that she comes out on the pitch and no matter who she plays against, she’s just going to play and she’s comfortable. I hope to see that next week.”
